name: Races
intro: **Every race question is a speed ratio in disguise.** "A beats B by x metres in a d-metre race" means that in the same time A covers d while B covers d − x, so the speed ratio is d : (d − x) (§1).
Read the language carefully: a beat given as a distance and a beat given as a time are different data, and "gives a start" reverses who covers what (§2).

qs.q: In a 100 m race, A beats B by 20 m. When A finishes, how far has B run (in metres)?
qs.h: §2 — "beats by 20 m" describes where B is at the moment A finishes.
qs.s: B has covered 80 m.

qs.q: In a 500 m race, A beats B by 50 m. The ratio of their speeds is
qs.h: §3 — same time, so the speeds are in the ratio of the distances covered.

qs.q: In a 200 m race, A beats B by 25 m. If A runs at 8 m/s, find B's speed (in m/s).
qs.h: §3 — find A's time, then divide B's distance by that same time.
qs.s: A takes 200/8 = 25 s, in which B covers 175 m ⟹ B's speed = 7 m/s.

qs.q: In a 1 km race, A beats B by 100 m. At the same speeds, in a 2 km race A beats B by
qs.h: §3 — the speed ratio is fixed, so the beat distance scales with the race length.
qs.s: Speeds are 10 : 9 ⟹ when A covers 2000 m, B covers 1800 m ⟹ a beat of 200 m.

qs.q: In a 400 m race, A beats B by 40 m, and in a separate 400 m race B beats C by 50 m. By how many metres does A beat C in a 400 m race?
qs.h: §5 — chain the two speed ratios. Do not add the two beats.
qs.s: A : B = 10 : 9 and B : C = 8 : 7 ⟹ A : C = 80 : 63 ⟹ when A runs 400, C runs 315 ⟹ a beat of 85 m. (Adding 40 + 50 = 90 is the planted error.)

qs.q: In a 500 m race, A beats B by 10 seconds. If B takes 60 seconds, find A's time (in seconds).
qs.h: §4 — a beat in time is simply the difference of the two finishing times.

qs.q: In a 1000 m race, A beats B by 100 m or 10 seconds. B's speed is
qs.h: §4 — the two statements describe the same gap, so B covers those 100 m in those 10 seconds.

qs.q: In a 1000 m race, A beats B by 100 m or 10 seconds. Find A's time for the race (in seconds).
qs.h: §4 — get B's speed from the twin statement, then B's total time, then subtract the beat.
qs.s: B's speed = 10 m/s ⟹ B takes 100 s ⟹ A takes 90 seconds.

qs.q: In a 300 m race, A beats B by 30 m or 6 seconds. A's speed is
qs.h: §4 — B's speed comes from the twin statement; A's time is B's time minus 6 seconds.
qs.s: B: 30/6 = 5 m/s ⟹ B takes 60 s ⟹ A takes 54 s ⟹ A's speed = 300/54 = 5.56 m/s.

qs.q: A covers a 300 m course in 45 seconds and B in 60 seconds. By how many metres does A beat B?
qs.h: §4 — in A's 45 seconds, work out how far B has got.
qs.s: B covers 300 × 45/60 = 225 m ⟹ a beat of 75 m.

qs.q: In a 100 m race, A beats B by 10 m and B beats C by 10 m. By how many metres does A beat C?
qs.h: §5 — multiply the ratios, don't add the beats. The answer is deliberately not 20.
qs.s: A : B = 10 : 9 and B : C = 10 : 9 ⟹ when A runs 100, B is at 90 and C at 81 ⟹ a beat of 19 m.

qs.q: In a 200 m race, A beats B by 20 m and A beats C by 38 m. In a 180 m race, B beats C by
qs.h: §5 — express both B and C relative to A, then form the B : C ratio directly.
qs.s: B = 0.90A and C = 0.81A ⟹ B : C = 10 : 9 ⟹ in a 180 m race C reaches 162 ⟹ a beat of 18 m.

qs.q: In a 500 m race, A beats B by 50 m, and B beats C by 50 m in a 500 m race. By how many metres does A beat C over 500 m?
qs.h: §5 — again the product of the ratios.
qs.s: A : B = B : C = 10 : 9 ⟹ when A runs 500, B is at 450 and C at 405 ⟹ a beat of 95 m.

qs.q: A runs 1 km in 4 minutes 54 seconds and B in 5 minutes. In a 1 km race A beats B by
qs.h: §4 — convert both to seconds, then find B's position at A's finishing time.
qs.s: 294 s vs 300 s ⟹ B covers 1000 × 294/300 = 980 m ⟹ a beat of 20 m.

qs.q: A runs 5/4 as fast as B. If A gives B a head start of 60 m, how long (in metres) must the race be so that both finish together?
qs.h: §6 — a dead heat means equal times: A covers d while B covers d − 60.

qs.q: A can run 1 km in 3 minutes 10 seconds and B in 3 minutes 20 seconds. For a dead heat, the head start A must give B is
qs.h: §6 — the head start equals the beat A would otherwise inflict.
qs.s: 190 s vs 200 s ⟹ in 190 s B covers 950 m ⟹ head start = 50 m.

qs.q: In a 200 m race, A gives B a start of 10 seconds and still beats him by 20 m. If B's speed is 5 m/s, find A's time for the race (in seconds).
qs.h: §7 — B runs for A's time plus the 10-second start, and covers 180 m in that period.
qs.s: B covers 180 m at 5 m/s = 36 s of running ⟹ A's time = 36 − 10 = 26 seconds.

qs.q: A gives B a start of 20 m in a 100 m race and still wins by 5 m. The ratio of their speeds is
qs.h: §7 — B only has 80 m to cover, and finishes 5 m short of the line when A arrives.
qs.s: A covers 100 m while B covers 75 m ⟹ 4 : 3.

qs.q: In a 1000 m race A beats B by 50 m. In a race of the same distance where A instead gives B a head start of 50 m, by how many metres does A win? (Enter 0 for a dead heat.)
qs.h: §6 — the head start exactly cancels the advantage that produced the original beat.
qs.s: Speeds 20 : 19. B must cover 950 m; in A's 1000 m, B covers 19/20 × 1000 = 950 m ⟹ they finish together, so A wins by 0 m.

qs.q: In a game of 100 points, A can give B 20 points. In the time A scores 100, how many points does B score?
qs.h: §8 — "gives 20 points" means B is on 80 when A reaches 100.
qs.s: 80 points.

qs.q: In a game of 80 points, A can give B 10 points and C 20 points. In a game of 100 points, A can give C
qs.h: §8 — build the A : C ratio from the 80-point game, then rescale to 100.
qs.s: A : C = 80 : 60 = 4 : 3 ⟹ in a 100-point game C scores 75 ⟹ A gives 25 points.

qs.q: In a game of 100 points, A can give B 20 points and B can give C 25 points. How many points can A give C in a game of 100?
qs.h: §8 + §5 — chain the ratios exactly as with runners.
qs.s: A : B = 5 : 4 and B : C = 4 : 3 ⟹ A : C = 5 : 3 ⟹ C scores 60 ⟹ A gives 40 points.

qs.q: On a 400 m circular track, A and B run at 8 m/s and 6 m/s in the same direction from the same point. A first laps B after
qs.h: §9 — lapping means gaining a full circumference at the relative speed.

qs.q: In a race on a 500 m circular track, A completes 3 laps in the time B completes 2.5 laps. By how many metres does A beat B?
qs.h: §9 — the gap is half a lap.
qs.s: A covers 1500 m and B 1250 m ⟹ a beat of 250 m.

qs.q: In a 300 m race, A beats B by 30 m. Find the ratio of A's speed to B's speed, as a fraction.
qs.h: Distances covered in the same time.

qs.q: In a 400 m race, A beats B by 25 m and B beats C by 20 m. A beats C by
qs.h: Chain the ratios; the answer is deliberately not 45.
qs.s: A : B = 16 : 15 and B : C = 20 : 19 ⟹ when A runs 400, B is at 375 and C at 356.25 ⟹ a beat of 43.75 m.

qs.q: A runs 4/3 as fast as B. If A gives B a start of 30 m, how long (in metres) must the course be for a dead heat?
qs.h: Equal times: A covers d while B covers d − 30.

qs.q: In a 100 m race, A beats B by 4 seconds. If B takes 25 seconds, A's speed is
qs.h: Subtract to get A's time, then divide.

qs.q: In a game of 100 points, A can give B 25 points. In a game of 60 points, how many points can A give B?
qs.h: The ratio is fixed; only the target changes.
qs.s: A : B = 4 : 3 ⟹ in 60 points B scores 45 ⟹ A gives 15 points.

qs.q: The speeds of A and B are in the ratio 3 : 4. A is given a head start of 140 m and the race ends in a dead heat. The length of the course is
qs.h: Here the slower runner gets the start. A covers d − 140 while B covers d.

qs.q: In a 1 km race, A beats B by 40 m and A beats C by 76 m. By how many metres does B beat C in a 1 km race?
qs.h: Put both B and C against A first.
qs.s: B : C = 960 : 924 ⟹ when B runs 1000, C reaches 962.5 ⟹ a beat of 37.5 m. (76 − 40 = 36 is the planted error.)

qs.q: In a 200 m race, A gives B a start of 5 seconds and beats him by 10 m. If A's speed is 8 m/s, B's speed is
qs.h: B runs for A's time plus the 5-second start, and covers 190 m.
qs.s: A takes 25 s ⟹ B runs for 30 s covering 190 m ⟹ 6.33 m/s.

audit: not converting the beat into a speed ratio before doing anything else (§1, §3)
adding two beats instead of multiplying the two speed ratios (§5)
treating the distance-beat and time-beat as separate facts rather than as one shared gap (§4)
getting the direction of a head start backwards — the runner given the start covers less (§6, §7)
forgetting that a time head start extends the slower runner's running time
assuming a head start equal to the beat still leaves a winner; it produces a dead heat exactly
rescaling a points game by subtracting instead of by reapplying the ratio (§8)
confusing lapping with meeting, or losing a half-lap in the count (§9)
